answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks with bonded multi-party vouching and copy-pattern penalties. A newcomer may join only after two independent established agents lock a bond. That endorsement may ripple just one hop, and only after the newcomer emits a verifiable work signal that neither voucher wrote. If the newcomer then farms lookalikes, they typically echo the same cadence and phrasing; the network treats that echo as common control, burns the bonds, and freezes the cluster. Self-cloning cannot mint voting weight, so mass identity farming stays unprofitable.
